definition: Mutual bodily contact or touching between partners, typically as foreplay; reciprocal physical closeness.
notes: Form VI masdar of لمس indicating reciprocal action; neutral in medical and literary registers but sexually charged in context; lighter than genital-focused touching.

definition: Physical friction or rubbing between bodies; in sexual contexts refers to erotic body-to-body rubbing without penetration.
notes: Primary meaning is mechanical or social friction (الاحتكاك الاجتماعي = social friction); sexual use is entirely contextual; the physics register ironically lowers its crude score despite sexual application.

definition: Biting; in sexual contexts refers to erotic biting during foreplay or intercourse.
notes: The ordinary Arabic word for biting; sexual use is entirely contextual. sensation_play is the closest registry concept though erotic biting is not inherently BDSM; universally understood, minimal crude charge on its own.

definition: Deliberate sexual groping or feeling of a partner's body, typically targeting erogenous zones during foreplay.
notes: Carries ambiguity between consensual foreplay and unwanted touching depending on context; the same word appears in legal complaints about harassment and in erotic literature; contextual register shifts dramatically.

definition: Touching or caressing with the hands in a tender or sexual manner; sexual touching short of intercourse.
notes: Form V of لمس; implies deliberate, attentive touching; softer and more consensual in connotation than تحسس; used in literary erotica and medical discourse alike.

definition: Physical coquetry or affectionate bodily play; pleasurable physical pampering and tender physical interaction between partners.
notes: دلال alone denotes coquetry or indulged pampering; جسدي (bodily/physical) specifies its physical expression; the compound is descriptive and literary, lower in crude charge than most sexual vocabulary.

definition: Group sexual intercourse; a sexual gathering involving multiple participants engaging simultaneously.
notes: جماع is the standard MSA clinical term for sexual intercourse; جماعي means collective/communal; the compound is composed and descriptive rather than euphemistic; high crude score reflects extreme social taboo regardless of clinical phrasing.

definition: A sexual encounter involving exactly three people; threesome.
notes: Literally 'triple' or 'triadic'; functioning as a calque of English 'threesome'; recognition boosted by widespread Arabic-subtitled pornographic content and internet slang.

definition: Partner or spouse swapping between consenting couples for sexual purposes.
notes: Transparent descriptive compound: مبادلة = exchange, الأزواج = the spouses/couples; understood by educated speakers exposed to Western media; extremely taboo in Islamic social context; no colloquial shortening exists in wide use.

definition: Swinging; phonetic Arabic transliteration of the English term for consensual partner-swapping sexual activity among couples.
notes: Pure phonetic borrowing; understood primarily by younger, internet-connected, or Western-exposed speakers; exists alongside the descriptive native phrase مبادلة الأزواج; crude score lower than native equivalent because loanwords feel more distanced.

definition: Orgy; transliterated loanword for a sexual gathering involving multiple participants.
notes: Phonetic Arabic rendering of English 'orgy'; widely understood through internet and pornographic exposure; no competing native Arabic term in contemporary usage for exactly this concept; sometimes spelled أورجية.

definition: Romantic flirtation or courtship; also the name of a venerable Arabic and Persian poetic genre devoted to erotic love, longing, and the beauty of the beloved.
notes: Polysemous and deeply prestigious: as a genre, the ghazal is one of the highest literary forms; as an act, it means making romantic overtures; no crude connotation whatsoever in MSA; sexual charge is sublimated into aesthetic pleasure.

definition: Flirting or making amorous overtures; active courtship involving playful or romantic advances.
notes: Form III verbal noun from the same root as غزل; the Form III pattern emphasizes mutuality or competition between parties, so مغازلة implies the transactional back-and-forth of flirtation rather than a solo performance.

definition: Seduction or enticement; drawing someone toward a sexual encounter by appealing to desire.
notes: Used in both religious discourse (enticement to sin) and everyday sexual contexts; less morally loaded than إغواء; the seducer in إغراء exploits appeal, while culpability for the outcome is shared.

definition: Seduction that leads another person morally astray; temptation with an implication of moral corruption or ruination.
notes: Stronger moral charge than إغراء; closely associated with Shaytan leading humans to sin; in sexual contexts the seducer bears full moral culpability for corrupting the other; the word implies the victim was diverted from virtue.

definition: Making persistent sexual overtures or advances upon someone; repeated attempts to seduce.
notes: Carries enormous Quranic resonance: Surat Yusuf (12:23–26) uses مراودته عن نفسه to describe Zulaykha's repeated attempts to seduce Joseph; any Arabic speaker with Quranic literacy hears this story in the word; uniquely combines high literary gravity with explicit sexual meaning.

definition: Gradually luring or drawing someone into a sexual or romantic situation through incremental steps and inducements.
notes: Root meaning: to draw someone step by step (درج = to step); in Quranic commentary refers to God's gradual testing of the disobedient; in contemporary usage describes methodical manipulation toward a goal; breadcrumbing is the closest registry match but استدراج implies deliberate escalating strategy, closer to grooming.

definition: Coquetry; the pleasurable, knowing flirtatiousness of one who is desired and who performs that desirability with artful indulgence.
notes: Untranslatable nuance: dalāl implies a self-indulgent, pampered quality — the person performing dalāl knows they are adored and luxuriates in it; wholly positive in classical Arabic poetics; completely distinct from wanton or promiscuous behavior.

definition: Acting coy or coquettish; the behavioral enactment of dalāl — adopting an affectedly charming, indulged manner to attract or retain affection.
notes: Verbal-act form of دلال; captures the performative, deliberate dimension of coquettish display; implies the agent is consciously performing for an admiring audience; socially acceptable and even admired behavior in many Arab cultural contexts.

definition: The specific physical and vocal affectations of coquetry — the lilting voice, the affected gait, the studied glance — through which sexual attractiveness is performed.
notes: More granular than دلال: غنج refers to the outward gestures and mannerisms constituting coquettish performance rather than the underlying disposition; a technical term of classical Arabic erotic poetics; lower recognition than دلال due to its more specialized literary register.

definition: Rape; the act of forcibly compelling sexual intercourse or penetration upon a non-consenting person.
notes: The standard modern Arabic legal and journalistic term for rape; from غصب (to seize by force); ravishment is archaic in English but maps to the same concept — the registry lacks a modern rape entry; extreme crude score despite clinical register because the act itself is maximally transgressive.

definition: Sexual harassment; unwanted sexual conduct — verbal, physical, or gestural — directed at a person without consent.
notes: Gained massive international recognition after 2011–2013 Tahrir Square mass-assault documentation under the term 'taharrush jama'i'; تحرش alone = harassment, جنسي = sexual; a clinical/legal compound now ubiquitous in Arab media, law, and activism.

definition: Sexual coercion; the use of force, threats, or sustained pressure to compel sexual acts from an unwilling person.
notes: إكراه carries rich Islamic jurisprudential history — it is a formal legal category (coercion that negates liability) — so the compound inherits a precise legal register; covers a spectrum from psychological pressure to physical compulsion, legally intermediate between harassment and rape.

definition: Sexual violation or abuse; any act that transgresses a person's bodily integrity and sexual autonomy without consent.
notes: انتهاك = violation/transgression from نهك (to exhaust, despoil); broader than اغتصاب — encompasses molestation, abuse, and non-penetrative violations; preferred in human rights, NGO, and advocacy discourse precisely because its breadth avoids narrowing harm to penetrative rape.

definition: Sexual assault; a physical attack of a sexual nature carried out against a person without consent.
notes: اعتداء = assault/aggression from عدا (to transgress, go beyond limits); the standard Arabic legal term corresponding to 'sexual assault' in criminal codes across Arab jurisdictions; emphasizes the aggressive, physical-attack character of the act more than انتهاك جنسي.
